source_refs.note: Oxidation of carboxylic acids: a main subheading of 23.5 Reactions of Carboxylic Acids, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 110-111.

blocks.text: Methanoic acid gets oxidized with both weak as well as strong oxidizing agents due to its structure and, hence, acts as a strong reducing agent.

blocks.alt: Methanoic acid, H-C(=O)-OH, drawn twice. On the left the H-C=O part is boxed, with an arrow to 'Aldehydic portion (-CHO) responsible for its behaviour as a powerful reducing agent.' On the right the C(=O)-OH part is boxed, with an arrow to 'Carboxylic portion (-COOH) responsible for its acidic character.'
blocks.caption: The aldehydic and carboxylic portions of methanoic acid (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 111).

blocks.text: Methanoic acid is the only monocarboxylic acid which gives positive silver mirror test (Tollen's test) and brick red precipitates with Fehling's solution. These reactions are used for the identification of methanoic acid.

blocks.title: Oxidation
blocks.text:
1. Loss of H₂ or (H⁻)
2. Addition of O or O₂
3. Addition of X₂
4. Loss of electrons
5. Increase in Ox. State
The oxidation of ethanedioic acid with acidified KMnO₄ or K₂Cr₂O₇ results in the formation of carbon dioxide and water.
